LHX.sentence: L3Harris has pulled back a fair bit from its high, and its profit margins are running thinner than the bigger defense companies', but steady military spending means the underlying business is fine — it just looks beaten down right now.

ASML.sentence: ASML ticked up a little, and while the stock looks expensive at first glance, that's misleading because their newest chipmaking machines are just starting to bring in real money.

LIN.sentence: No fresh news on Linde today — the industrial gas business just keeps quietly humming along.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quiet and only slightly off its high — the AI cloud story keeps grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is steady, and there's an encouraging sign underneath: money is starting to flow back into biotech again, which usually means more lab equipment orders for them a few quarters down the road.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is barely moved — it's essentially a toll road for oil and gas, paying a solid dividend, and there's nothing unusual happening either way.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow dipped a touch and has come well off its high, but big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its workflow and AI tools on long contracts, so the business is still growing strongly.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore lagged today even as copper prices climbed — since copper is a big chunk of its profits, that gap suggests the shares may be due to catch up.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta drifted down slightly, but the price it charges per ton of crushed stone is still climbing steadily, which is the part that really matters — a headline drop in reported prices is just a distortion from product mix, not the business weakening.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is calm, and a strong Mexican peso is quietly helping, since most of this Latin American Coke bottler's earnings are in pesos.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is flat today, but with oil selling far above what it costs them to pump it, there's plenty of cash flowing to fund its very generous dividend.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the container shipping giant, dropped nearly 4% today, yet its shares are priced below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace — a sign the market may be too gloomy on global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard slipped a hair and is trading barely above Visa despite usually commanding a premium, even as people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company is flat today but sits far below its high — an unusually rare discount on a market leader while hospitals keep doing more procedures on its machines.
